script.analysis: All 20,775 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: Home Depot checkout and new-homeowner repairs (AC $7,000, roof $4,500, water heater $1,800 = $13,300 in 8 months). Statistics: $526B renovation spending vs Sweden GDP; Bankrate 2025 $21,400/year hidden costs; 1% rule vs 2-3% spending; 46% with >$5K surprises; NerdWallet first-year repairs; state/metro hidden-cost figures; property tax averages and NJ vs FL example; non-mortgage cost growth; HOA prevalence and fee increases; special assessments; condo cost stack; South Florida condos vs rent; Indian River County cash sales; repeated maintenance and repair statistics (second half largely repeats the first); pre-1960 homes 8%; HGTV renovation creep; New England vs East South Central costs; $400K house vs renting with investing the difference; close: rent and invest, run the math. Heavily one-sided toward renting, statistic-dense, repetitive, few sources named precisely. ASR artifacts ("$18 in 2019" for HOA, "$3,18", "$69,000", "12% phase one") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:10400 $7,000 + $4,500 + $1,800 = $13,300 correct. "$526 billion ... more than the entire GDP of Sweden" is wrong: Sweden's GDP is roughly $600B. Bankrate 2025 hidden homeownership costs ~$21,400/year ($1,783/month) correctly cited, but that figure already includes property taxes, insurance, maintenance and utilities - the script says it is "on top of" insurance, maintenance and taxes, double-counting. State (Hawaii ~$34.6K, West Virginia ~$12.6K; ratio ~2.75x) and metro figures are consistent with Bankrate-style tables. Average property tax ~$3,500 is below ATTOM's ~$4,000+ national average; $3,500/12 = $291 correct. NJ $400K at ~2.23% = $8,920 vs FL ~0.82% = $3,280, difference ~$470/month correct.

0:10400 "Non-mortgage costs jumped 30% in 2025 alone" unsupported. HOA "median rose from $18 in 2019 to $135 ... 25%" is garbled (likely $108 -> $135 = 25%). Special assessments "no vote, no discussion, pay or lose your home" overgeneralizes; HOA governance and lien/foreclosure rules vary by state.

10400:20775 "Homes built before 1960 cost 8% of home value to maintain annually" ($24,000 on $300K) is implausible as an average and unsourced. Maintenance $3,018 + emergency $2,321 = $5,339 (stored "$3,18" ASR) consistent. $400K house, 20% down, $320K at 7%: P&I ~$2,129, matches $2,130; $3,413 x 12 = $40,956 correct. "$80,000 invested 30 years at 7% grows to $69,000" is wrong (~$609,000; likely garbled), and the renter's $1.6M omits that $609K while using $1,413/month (which gives ~$1.72M at 7%). The comparison assumes rent stays flat for 30 years while ownership costs include rising taxes/fees, ignores that the mortgage payment is fixed and ends, and values the home at $850K (2.5%/yr) - a one-sided setup.
